title: Running YC like a founder: lean vs fat startups, listening to customers, and AI-era moats
summary: Garry Tan talks to Jack Altman about running YC with zero-based accounting and founder energy. He covers how to advise founders, what makes a great founder, when to raise big versus stay lean, and how AI changes team size but not moats.

principles.text: Raise big only if elite investors back you; otherwise start lean, because lean is how you earn the right to go fat.
principles.quote: how would you even get to the point where you could be a fat startup? Well, you got to do it lean.

principles.text: The best founders are the best listeners; pulling requirements from customers early turns into customers pulling product later, which is product market fit.
principles.quote: basically that yanking turns into like they're pushing like and that's product market fit.

principles.text: Advise as a soft advisor, not a boss. Spiky, even wrong, advice beats median advice founders can get from any podcast.
principles.quote: what's really valuable is to have people around who have seen enough and are intuitive enough about like ideas and technology and teams that they can give you even spiky advice

principles.text: AI changes how big a team you need, not the moats. Switching costs, proprietary data, brand and network effects still decide winners.
principles.quote: the moes are all the same, right? Like switching cost, data that like, you know, you have access to that nobody else has.

principles.text: Early on, most of the value of an advisor or investor is helping you avoid the many ways startups die.
principles.quote: there's like a billion ways to die.

principles.text: Build a shelling point for talented builders and the capital, customers and knowledge follow. Culture is everything, so be willing to prune.
principles.quote: The world needs shelling points for um for builders for talented people and then their capital exists, their customers exist
